title: docs(s1.3): CCF near-tie logging, CPU vs CUDA local alignment (evidence only)
head: ccf-near-tie-logging
body:
S1.3 / S1.3b (#238): the evidence identifies near-tie amplification, avoidable peak-fit arithmetic loss, and an inverse-FFT input-contract problem. S1 cannot be explained as ordinary float32 CPU/CUDA rounding alone. This PR contains diagnostic evidence only; it does not implement or validate a production fix, establish complete causal attribution, or establish which backend is scientifically better.

## Findings and limits

- **Near-tie amplification in the five S1-positive cases.** All nine S1-relevant patches first meet the diagnostic separation criterion (candidate shifts differing by more than 0.5 px) at different integer CCF peak choices. In seven, the candidates are ≤16 ulps apart on both maps; in two, one map is tied or within 3 ulps while the other has a 36–68-ulp lead. This describes a nonlinear amplification mechanism, not the first arithmetic difference in the pipeline. The 10216 3×3 case reaches relative RMSE 0.196 with all nine patches accepted; swapping patch (2,1)'s observations in the fit reduces field differences from 1.81/0.515 to 0.79/0.146 px (max/rms).

- **Avoidable arithmetic loss on identical native-captured inputs.** At 10216 global iteration 1, frame 56, CPU and CUDA select the same pixel and have identical five float32 CCF samples, yet their native x candidates differ by 0.00794319 px because of peak-curvature evaluation precision/order. Host scalar replay reproduces all 32,195 captured CUDA candidates exactly. Using the stable float32 denominator (vp-m)+(vn-m) reduces the largest same-input candidate-component difference from promoted evaluation from 0.135252 px to 0.000002646 px, with no guard changes in this captured set. This is replay of native captures, **not a native run of a modified kernel or an end-to-end cure**. [Arithmetic review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/250#pullrequestreview-5573028636).

- **A systematic upstream inverse-FFT problem in S1.3b.** For 10216 and 12963, equal nominal global trajectories produce near-equal full spectra but substantially different reconstructed real frames. Fractional shifts leave non-Hermitian boundary data. [CUDA 12.8's C2R contract](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types) requires Hermitian input; behavior is undefined otherwise. This is an application representation/input-contract issue, not an established cuFFT library defect. The measured row term predicts the equal-trajectory **low-frequency patch-window** difference to ≤5.8e-7 in the 150 checked patch-frames. It does not explain the entire full-band image difference: after optimal row-mean removal, frame 11 retains relative residuals of 1.07e-4 (10216) and 3.01e-4 (12963). A second, alternating-x component associated with the kx=0 boundary remains a hypothesis. [Contract and residual review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/250#pullrequestreview-5573621228).

- **Partial causal separation, not closure.** CPU trajectory injection into CUDA leaves the 12963 near-tie divergences and relative RMSE 0.4999, while 10216 falls to 0.021. Same-backend trajectory controls support shift/crop geometry as the source of the measured amplitude residual. A native Hermitian-repair/removal control has not yet established how much of the remaining flips or published-image discrepancy comes from the inverse-FFT defect. Small own-input CCF-map errors (≤9.4 ulps) and windowed phase errors do not exclude the separately demonstrated scalar arithmetic or boundary-contract issues. [Attribution review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/250#pullrequestreview-5573056916).

- **Fit amplification is distinct from solver failure.** Common-accepted-patch refits sharply reduce field disagreement in three 5×5 cases. The audited designs are full rank; scaled and unscaled float64 fits agree closely. Coarse STAR coefficient formatting explains the apparent up-to-0.38 px refit-versus-serialized-model discrepancy. Published fit counterfactuals use fresh refits of rounded STAR observations, not exact in-memory native coefficients or regenerated images. [Fit review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/250#pullrequestreview-5573092421).

## Still open

- Native same-input and end-to-end controls separating stable peak arithmetic, Hermitian repair, estimator feedback and final reconstruction.
- Validation of both self-conjugate boundary columns at the relevant C2R sites. Reduced-grid CCF cropping introduces a separate source-level conjugacy risk; it is **not yet a measured additional S1 cause**. [CCF-boundary review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/250#pullrequestreview-5573645810).
- Whether and how the defects reach published products, including the separate dose-weighted reconstruction path; complete attribution beyond the sampled movies/frames.
- The appropriate interpolation/repair policy and downstream CTF/FSC/B-factor consequences in S1.4. CPU agreement is a Tier B reference, not scientific ground truth. Existing gates and tolerances remain unchanged.

## Proposed fix and validation plan

**Proposal only: none of the changes below is implemented or validated by this PR.** Start with two independently testable changes; keep peak selection/tie rules, convergence thresholds and existing acceptance/image gates fixed.

1. **Stabilize the scalar peak fit.** In `findPeakAndInterpolateKernel`, compare the minimal float32 change `denom = (vp-m) + (vn-m)` with promoting the five selected samples to double before any quadratic-fit arithmetic, then casting the final output. Preserve the current scale for the first same-input comparison. Test both on-device against the retained native captures and a promoted same-sample oracle. Include exactly flat and one-ULP plateaus, search-boundary neighbors above the winner, positive/negative curvature, values around the existing `1e-15f` guard, subnormals, overflow-range and non-finite inputs. Guard equivalence must not be assumed: with `m=vp=1` and `vn=1-2^-24`, the original float denominator rounds to zero while the difference form gives nonzero curvature. Specify the intended fallback explicitly. Test the actual Release compiler/flags, contraction, reassociation and flush-to-zero behavior; use explicit rounding operations if needed to preserve the chosen evaluation order. This cannot recover CCF contrast already lost before the fit.

2. **Make every C2R input satisfy a documented real-image policy.** For a diagnostic candidate, project each self-conjugate boundary column of the actual inverse geometry: `kx=0`, and `kx=Nx/2` only when Nx is even. For each column set `H[y,c] = (F[y,c] + conj(F[(-y) mod Ny,c]))/2`; self-paired rows 0 and, for even Ny, Ny/2 must be real. Implement each conjugate pair without an in-place read/write race. Preserve interior bins and legitimate complex conjugate-paired boundary signal; do not zero whole columns or every boundary imaginary component. Projection restores the input invariant, but choosing a scientifically appropriate Nyquist interpolation/resampling convention remains a separate decision. For example, at an even-by-even checkerboard corner, phase-then-project gives a factor `cos(pi*(dx+dy))`, while a separable real-Nyquist convention gives `cos(pi*dx)*cos(pi*dy)`. Both match integer shifts; use a pure checkerboard test to expose the fractional-shift policy choice. For reduced-grid CCFs, explicitly define how the original positive/negative Nyquist partners are folded and scaled: projecting a truncated buffer alone does not reconstruct an omitted source partner. Check every new cutoff edge, including the y-Nyquist row at interior kx, and the corners; single-mode amplitude/phase and parity-changing resize tests are needed even when the buffer passes the Hermitian check.

   Audit all inverse consumers on both backends, including global reconstruction into patch inputs, the actual reduced-grid CCF after construction, and all output reconstruction paths. In particular, `computeGlobalInverseFFT` copies resident spectra into `d_inverse_tile`, whereas the dose-weighted path later reads the original resident `d_Fframes` into a different weighted scratch buffer. Repairing only the global scratch leaves that later C2R input unrepaired. For the first causal controls, project the relevant consumption scratch without silently changing resident spectra or cumulative-shift semantics; repeated projection after every incremental shift is a different operator and needs its own justification. The cropped-CCF concern remains a source-level risk until measured.

3. **Separate the causes with native ablations before combining fixes.** First feed identical saved map/spectrum bytes to the native kernels, using fresh copies where C2R overwrites its input. For inverse tests, compare CPU/GPU C2R after the same boundary policy with an explicitly defined high-precision real-valued Fourier reference; include isolated DC/Nyquist modes, integer and fractional x-only/y-only/combined shifts, and even/odd geometries. Report full-band residuals and low-CCF-window residuals separately. Then run baseline/global-only/local-only/both stable-curvature arms; independently test inverse repair at global reconstruction, CCF construction and product reconstruction, followed by the combined candidate. Freeze movie inputs, recipes, device and build settings. Log first divergent samples/candidates, final trajectories, exact accepted patch sets, full-precision model coefficients, and dose-weighted and unweighted image metrics. Fixed-trajectory reconstruction controls distinguish estimator feedback from direct output artifacts.

4. **Choose the production policy from correctness, science and cost.** Add known-truth synthetic motion tests that exercise the selected real-valued Nyquist convention, alongside retained real movies and S1.4 CTF/FSC/B-factor comparisons. CPU agreement is useful regression evidence, not ground truth. Do not relax gates or declare S1 closed solely because a trajectory or RMSE improves. Measure kernel and whole-movie runtime, memory/workspace, extra launches and synchronization on the intended GPUs; do not assume either selective FP64 or projection is free. Advance a production change only with reproducible native correctness results, quantified remaining failures and the scientific/performance trade-off recorded.

## Evidence and provenance

Evidence: [docs/post_rc0/s1/ccf_ties/README.md](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/7fc9733f3b02cd34f7dd3dde7e8a89e7ed7ff1bf/docs/post_rc0/s1/ccf_ties/README.md), retained raw records and analysis, plus the review qualifications above.

- Frozen production source F: 6d68e2d6. Diagnostic branch diag/s1-ccf-ties: 9283ff7a (CCF records), 61c3a85e (trajectory capture/override), and c8fa55f5 (full-frame dumps). Diagnostic diffs are retained as evidence and are not production changes.
- Initial campaign: 30/30 runs exit 0; 20/20 diagnostic neutrality comparisons match production MRC core headers, pixel payloads and per-movie STARs. Extended headers also match; timestamp-bearing MRC labels are excluded.
- S1.3b: 16/16 runs exit 0; 12/12 retained identity comparisons pass, covering own-trajectory controls and added instrumentation.
- Native campaigns ran on 4GPUs, lane GPU2, Release builds, under the recorded GPU lock and eight-CPU cap. CUDA runs are UUID-witnessed. Host replays and fit analyses are identified separately from native execution.

Docs-only and open for review. No production source, default, gate or tolerance changes; no timing or scientific-outcome claim. No merge is requested.

comments.body:
The new native captures expose an avoidable arithmetic effect in the peak path itself. This is stronger evidence than the toy example in #232, so I would qualify “no CUDA defect found” / “all rounding” before treating S1.3 as causal closure.

Concrete same-input witness at this head: raw/runs/e10216-p3-diag-{cpu,cuda}-on/ccf.txt.gz, global iteration 1, frame 56. Both backends select (0,0); all five captured float32 map samples are bit-identical. For x, m=36366.4296875, vp=36365.69140625, vn=36366.359375, with scale=4. The existing CUDA expression rounds vp+vn before subtracting 2*m, producing denominator -0.8125; evaluating the identical stored samples in double gives -0.80859375. Native CUDA x=-1.6442307233810425; native CPU x=-1.6521739130434783. This 0.00794319 px difference needs neither different FFT samples nor an integer peak/tie change.

I replayed all 32,195 CUDA records, including retries, converting the nine-significant-digit samples back to float32 and using the logged patch sizes/CCF dimensions, holding the GPU's float32 scale fixed across variants:
- Explicit float32 evaluation of the existing expression reproduces every recorded native x/y candidate exactly.
- Replacing only the denominator with (vp-m)+(vn-m), retaining float32 throughout and the same winner/guard/scale, gives the exact double denominator on all 64,390 recorded axes.
- Largest absolute candidate-component difference from the double evaluation of the same samples falls from 0.13525164 px to 0.000002646 px. The larger example is 10474F3 patch (1,5), iteration 4, frame 6; its retry repeats it.
- Already in global iteration 1, the largest same-input component effect is 0.0170694 px (10641b, reference frame 1). For 10216 it is the 0.00794319 px witness above.
- No guard branch changes, non-finite values, or zero-denominator repairs occurred in this captured set. One search-boundary record has a neighbor above the selected maximum; it was included, not discarded.

These are host scalar replays of native captured samples, not a native run of a proposed fix. They isolate avoidable evaluation-order loss on an already-quantized CCF; they do not measure the unknown unquantized peak, prove the entire S1 mismatch is fixed, or remove the observed near-tie mechanism. In the key 10216 (2,1), iteration 2, frame 1 event, the corresponding same-input y correction is only 0.00844582 px, much smaller than that event's different-integer-peak jump.

A useful next paired experiment is current expression vs stable float32 differences vs promoting just the five samples/fit to double, from identical captured maps first and then through the complete iterative run with unchanged tie rules, convergence threshold and image gates. Please include exactly flat/one-ULP plateaus, ties, search-boundary neighbors, near-guard/subnormal inputs and compiler reassociation in a regression check before choosing an implementation. The finite captured set is not a proof of universal guard equivalence. This should let us distinguish ordinary backend map differences from this separately demonstrated, avoidable arithmetic contribution.

A separate attribution/scope point from the analysis scripts: the evidence supports the near-tie mechanism, but the current “patch-input differences are the global trajectory difference, propagated” and “phase shift is not the cause” wording is stronger than the measured controls.

1. phasefit.py reports hypot(fitted_translation + global_trajectory_delta). That is agreement between two translation estimates, not the residual phase left after fitting. It does not measure the component of phase error orthogonal to the two translation columns. The committed direct ramp test makes this important: summary.json reports 12963 input relative difference 0.00635078 before versus 0.00620990 after correction, and 10474F3 0.00590086 versus 0.00580159. Those aggregate medians retain about 97.8% and 98.3% of the original difference. This does not disprove the proposed crop explanation, but it does leave it untested. Please label the quoted “residual px” as translation-estimate disagreement and also report a weighted phase-fit residual.

2. analyze.py shift_test only evaluates a transition when the next iteration's input exists. Consequently the final shift of a converged global iteration is outside this test, as are frequencies outside the CCF window. That final full spectrum is what the subsequent global inverse FFT and patch crop consume (runner around 3404–3488 and 3792–3802). Spatial cropping mixes frequencies, so the reported <=5.7e-7 inter-iteration window error is not a bound on the full upstream operation that supplies patch inputs.

The discriminating control is a 2x2 replay from one shared full-frame spectrum: CPU/CUDA shift-and-reconstruction operators crossed with the two prescribed global trajectories, followed by identical crop/group/FFT. Holding trajectory fixed separates backend arithmetic; swapping trajectory on one backend measures propagation including crop amplitude changes. This would turn the currently inferred link into a measured one.

Two targeted follow-ons now have unusually strong motivation:
- For the demonstrated curvature effect, a native same-map test followed by GPU baseline/global-only/local-only/both stable-curvature diagnostic arms would distinguish upstream seeding from late local contribution. Keep the existing selection, convergence and output gates.
- For DC conditioning, both CPU and CUDA retain the DC term in the leave-one-out CCF. Zero only the CCF spectrum's (0,0) term before inverse FFT as a diagnostic control. In exact arithmetic this only subtracts a spatial constant and preserves peak locations/quadratic curvature. In float32, the retained pedestal can lose contrast before the selector sees it; the README's “uniform offset cannot change ... quadratic step” needs that exact-arithmetic qualification. Subtracting the mean after the float32 inverse cannot recover contrast already lost.

The scalar result in my earlier review was also independently checked with a separate struct.pack/unpack float32 implementation directly on the raw records: every native candidate reproduced, and the same denominator/guard results held. None of these replays is a native run of the proposed changes.

Fit-level cross-check: I reproduced the published counterfactuals from the ten production STARs and added a common-accepted-patch control. On the same 33x33 grid/all-frame definition, restricting both refits to the intersection of accepted patches changes max/rms field differences as follows:
- 10216 5x5: 7.401/1.628 -> 0.221/0.033 px.
- 10474F3: 7.445/1.578 -> 0.053/0.015 px.
- 10641: 94.323/18.403 -> 0.400/0.075 px.
- 12963: 9.477/1.479 -> 3.187/0.668 px; substantial differences in common accepted trajectories remain.
- 10216 3x3 is unchanged, as expected because all nine patches are common.

This supports acceptance-set/model extrapolation sensitivity as a major downstream amplifier in three 5x5 cases. It is not evidence that the 94 px field difference is a least-squares arithmetic error. Every fitted design has rank 18; column-normalized condition numbers are about 202–365, and column-scaled versus unscaled float64 refits differ by <3e-10 px on this grid. These remain host fit-only controls; corrected images have not been regenerated.

There is also a specific explanation for the up-to-0.38 px refit_reproduces_star discrepancy. metadata_table.cpp:257–276 formats negative doubles with only five digits after the decimal (scientific only below magnitude 0.001 or above 100000). In the 10641 CPU STAR, coefficient index 8, x²z³, is stored as -0.00122; the refit gives -0.00122271287007. Applying the writer's exact formatting to the refit reduces its field discrepancy against the stored STAR from 0.356601 to 0.000122 px on CPU and from 0.382139 to 0.000200 px on CUDA. Cubic time dependence makes this serialization loss visible.

Please distinguish the quantities explicitly: fitattr.py:86–89 computes cpu_vs_cuda and swaps from fresh refits of rounded STAR observations; only refit_reproduces_star compares those fits with serialized coefficients. For an exact native-model check, capture full-precision in-memory coefficients before STAR formatting. The serialization loss is a separate round-trip concern, not an explanation for the already-written native MRC mismatch. Reporting common-patch refits and full-image versus observed-patch-region fields would make the acceptance/extrapolation mechanism especially clear.

Reviewed the S1.3b delta at 7fc9733f. The 16 retained runs all exit 0, all eight CUDA runs witness the intended UUID, and all 12 retained identity comparisons pass. The equal-trajectory/full-spectrum controls materially improve the diagnosis. Two details matter before implementing a remedy.

1. This is an input-contract problem, not a demonstrated cuFFT library defect. The CUDA 12.8 documentation explicitly requires Hermitian input for multidimensional C2R and says behavior is undefined otherwise: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types . Fractionally phase-shifting the stored boundary columns without restoring their conjugacy can violate that precondition in exact arithmetic. The native row term is therefore evidence of a real application-level numerical/representation issue; it should not be classified as ordinary float32 roundoff or as a portable property of cuFFT. “Present whenever x-shift is fractional” also needs qualification: its size depends on the Nyquist content and can vanish.

2. The full-frame residual is not entirely a row constant. In raw/s13b/analysis/*-fullframe.json, frame 11 has after_removing_row_means_rms:
- 10216: 0.0036416573, or 1.0696e-4 relative to frame RMS.
- 12963: 0.0003972494, or 3.0129e-4 relative.
Subtracting the row mean is the least-squares best possible row-only correction, so these are lower bounds for subtracting any h(y) from that CPU/CUDA real-frame difference. Both records also show a non-Hermitian kx=0 column. The <=5.8e-7 hpredict residual concerns cropped low-frequency CCF-window spectra and cannot certify the full image. Please retain separate low-window and full-band residual claims, and identify the source/metric for the README's 2e-6/6e-8 full-frame residual statement.

A targeted next native test would feed identical saved spectrum bytes to both inverse paths, then repeat after projecting BOTH self-conjugate boundary columns: kx=0, plus kx=nx/2 when nx is even. For each such column use H[ky]=(F[ky]+conj(F[-ky mod ny]))/2; self-paired ky=0 and, when even, ny/2 become real. Preserve the legitimate Hermitian component rather than zeroing the whole Nyquist column. First compare to the explicitly defined real-valued reference, then rerun the equal-trajectory patch/acceptance/product controls. Include integer/fractional x-only, y-only and combined shifts, even/odd dimensions, and isolated boundary modes.

The additional full-band residual may be an alternating-x component associated with the kx=0 violation; packed real-FFT algorithms can mix invalid DC/Nyquist imaginary components. That is a hypothesis to test with an isolated-mode witness, not a claim about cuFFT internals. Repairing only the observed h(y) after inverse could leave the C2R contract violation and other components intact.

The earlier same-input peak-curvature finding remains a separate demonstrated arithmetic contribution. These new controls do not yet quantify how much either mechanism contributes to the final scientific outcome.

One implementation-scope addition to the Hermitian check: please also instrument the actual reduced-grid CCF spectrum before its C2R, not just the full-frame global spectrum.

computeReferenceKernel/computeCCFKernel copy the original frequency window into the smaller ccf_nx/ccf_ny geometry (cuda_alignpatch.cu:140–179; corresponding CPU runner:4747–4772). A valid full-image Hermitian spectrum need not be valid at the new crop boundaries. For example, when cropping a 16-row spectrum to 8 rows, original ky=+4 becomes the new self-conjugate Nyquist row; its original conjugate at ky=-4 is not folded into that cell. At kx=0 the copied coefficient can therefore remain complex. The new last x column has the analogous conjugate-pair requirement. The kernels do not enforce those conditions before inverse.

This is a source-level contract risk, not a measured extra cause of S1: the B weights suppress boundary content, and the retained <=9.4-ulp own-input map comparisons remain valid observations. But fixing only the full-frame global inverse would not prove all C2R inputs are valid. Record conjugacy residuals at both actual CCF boundary columns and compare a boundary-projected same-buffer control, preserving all interior bins and existing gates. That will distinguish the measured global reconstruction problem from any smaller crop-boundary contribution without changing weights or guessing from total-map norms.
